hints: Identify the total group size: 4 men + 6 women = 10 people in total.
Calculate the total number of unrestricted committees of 5 people chosen from 10: $\binom{10}{5}$.
Calculate the number of forbidden committees containing BOTH William and Mary: choosing William, Mary, and 3 others from the remaining 8 people: $\binom{8}{3}$.
Subtract the forbidden count from the total count to find the valid committees.
walkthrough:
Calculate the total number of unrestricted committees of 5 chosen from 10 people:
$$\text{Total committees} = \binom{10}{5} = \dfrac{10 \times 9 \times 8 \times 7 \times 6}{5 \times 4 \times 3 \times 2 \times 1} = 252$$

Calculate the number of committees where BOTH William and Mary are chosen:
$$\text{Committees with both} = \binom{8}{3} = \dfrac{8 \times 7 \times 6}{3 \times 2 \times 1} = 56$$

Subtract the committees with both from the total to find the number of valid committees:
$$\text{Valid committees} = 252 - 56 = 196$$
teacher_walkthrough: A committee of 5 people is selected from a group of 10 people (4 men and 6 women). William is one of the men and Mary is one of the women.
The restriction states that William and Mary refuse to serve together on the committee. This means they cannot both be on the committee at the same time.

Use the complement subtraction method:
$$\text{Valid committees} = \text{Total unrestricted committees} - \text{Committees containing both William and Mary}$$

Step 1: Compute total unrestricted committees from 10 people:
$$\binom{10}{5} = \frac{10!}{5! \, 5!} = \frac{10 \times 9 \times 8 \times 7 \times 6}{120} = 252$$

Step 2: Compute committees that include both William and Mary.
William and Mary occupy 2 of the 5 places, so we must choose the remaining $5 - 2 = 3$ members from the other $10 - 2 = 8$ people:
$$\binom{8}{3} = \frac{8 \times 7 \times 6}{3 \times 2 \times 1} = 56$$

Step 3: Subtract the forbidden committees from the total:
$$\text{Valid committees} = 252 - 56 = 196$$
